title: Al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya fi al-Siyasa al-Shar'iyya
author: ibn-qayyim
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Ibn Qayyim's treatise on how a judge may establish the truth: circumstantial evidence, the testimony of different kinds of witness, oaths, documents and the discretion of the ruler, with the market inspector's office and the policing of public life.
historicalContext: The work defends the use of evidence beyond formal testimony, arguing that justice is the aim of the law and that any method that reveals it belongs to the law. It is a key text for the history of Islamic judicial procedure.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
